steps.say: The bladder plate is exposed by failed midline fusion. The cloacal membrane is left without mesoderm reinforcement. Lateral mesoderm is staged failing to grow inward on schedule. The weak membrane is staged rupturing before the sixth week. The open bladder template is staged everting onto the belly. Associated defects are staged following the same field error.
steps.tx: **Cloacal membrane** (belly wall seal) rupture before the **6th week** (sixth gestational week) follows failed reinforcement by **lateral mesoderm** (side body wall tissue) ingrowth. The unstable membrane bursts early and everts the bladder plate. Counsel parents antenatally when diagnosed, because delivery planning starts before birth.

steps.say: The defect list is recognized at delivery routinely. An open bladder template is exposed on the belly. The pubic bones are spread by wide diastasis. Rectus muscles are staged diverging around the defect. Epispadias is staged opening the urethra dorsally. The umbilicus is staged sitting low near the plate.
steps.tx: **Bladder template** (open bladder plate) with splayed **pubic diastasis** (spread pubic bones), divergent rectus muscles, **epispadias** (dorsal urethral opening), and low-set umbilicus defines the complex. Document every element at birth. Photograph for records with consent, because staged plans reference baseline anatomy always.

steps.say: Classic repair is staged proceeding in three stages. Closure with osteotomy is performed within seventy two hours. Epispadias repair is scheduled at one to two years. Bladder neck reconstruction is booked at four to five years. The Young Dees Leadbetter technique is used for the neck. Continence is constructed stepwise alongside growth.
steps.tx: **Classic staged repair** (three step rebuild) closes bladder and abdominal wall with **pelvic osteotomy** (pelvic bone cut) within **72 hours** (seventy two hours), repairs epispadias at **1 to 2 years** (one to two years), and rebuilds the neck by **Young-Dees-Leadbetter** (bladder neck tightening) at **4 to 5 years** (four to five years). Hinge each stage on growth and capacity, because rushing fails.

steps.say: Bone work is staged making soft closure possible. Bilateral pelvic osteotomy is added to late closures. Closure beyond seventy two hours is staged needing bone cuts. Posterior iliac with anterior innominate cuts are the options. Pubic bones are brought together without tension. Wires with external fixation are staged holding the ring.
steps.tx: **Bilateral pelvic osteotomy** (both side bone cuts) is mandatory for closure beyond **72 hours** (seventy two hours) to deliver **tension-free closure** (slack midline join). Posterior iliac, anterior innominate, or horizontal cuts re-approximate pubis. Fix the ring and nurse immobilized, because bone healing sets soft success.

steps.say: Some centres are staged finishing everything neonatally here. Complete primary repair is performed in one sitting only. The Mitchell technique is credited for this approach. Bladder closure with epispadias repair is combined together. Bladder neck work is added in the same anaesthetic. Continence results are debated across centres still.
steps.tx: **CPRE** (single stage exstrophy fix) by the **Mitchell technique** (neonatal complete repair) combines bladder closure with epispadias and bladder neck work as **complete primary repair** (one sitting rebuild) in expert hands. Weigh single anaesthetic gain against redo risk. Follow continence long term, because early closure does not guarantee dryness.

steps.say: The Kelly operation is staged rebuilding the outlet anatomically here. Bladder neck with pelvic floor is reconstructed together. The external sphincter complex is wrapped around the urethra. Continence is restored without overtightening the outlet. Dissection is staged staying wide around nerves always. Function is tested carefully as healing completes.
steps.tx: **Kelly procedure** (anatomical outlet rebuild) reconstructs bladder neck with pelvic floor and **sphincter complex reconstruction** (muscle wrap repair) for anatomical continence without neck tightening. Preserve nerves in wide dissection. Test continence as tissues mature, because scarring shifts results over years of growth.

steps.say: Neck surgery is staged needing a proven reservoir first. Bladder capacity is measured carefully under anaesthesia. Eighty five to one hundred mL is required beforehand. Smaller bladders are grown with cycling first routinely. Formal reconstruction is booked only after proof of growth. Voluntary voiding is staged following adequate storage.
steps.tx: **Bladder capacity prerequisite** (size gate for neck surgery) demands at least **85 mL to 100 mL** (eighty five to one hundred millilitres) under anaesthesia before **bladder neck reconstruction** (continence tightening) for voluntary voiding. Cycle small bladders to grow them first. Re-measure before booking, because unready reservoirs fail.

steps.say: Cancer watch is staged never ending after repair always. Unclosed with reconstructed bladders are charged carrying lifelong risk here. Adenocarcinoma risk is raised four hundred fold lifelong. Glandular metaplasia is staged driving the malignant change. Cystitis glandularis is staged preceding malignant shift. Annual cystoscopy is scheduled for life routinely.
steps.tx: **Adenocarcinoma of bladder** (gland cancer) risk rises **400-fold** (four hundred times) lifelong in exstrophy bladders via **cystitis glandularis** (gland metaplasia) change. Survey reconstructed and unclosed bladders annually with cystoscopy and biopsy. Counsel lifelong watch at transition, because risk never expires with age.
